newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU monetary committee not seen meeting on lira.
newsitem.headline: EU monetary committee not seen meeting on lira.

text.p: The European Union's monetary committee is not expected to meet this weekend to consider Italy's re-entry into the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM), monetary sources said on Saturday.
"I haven't heard that (the committee) is planning a meeting," said one EU official familiar with the group's deliberations.

Speculation that Italy might join the ERM this weekend was fueled on Friday after Italian prime minister Romano Prodi said talks on the level at which the lira might re-enter the system should open "as soon as possible."

He was speaking after a meeting with French president Jacques Chirac, whose doubts over Italy's chances of qualifying for a single currency in 1999 nearly scuttled a planned summit between the two nations.
EU monetary officials said it was understandable that Italy would want enter the currency grid relatively soon given the lira's rapid appreciation in recent weeks.
"There is no reason for them to wait much longer," said one source, adding that it would not be unreasonable to see the lira re-enter the ERM within a month or so.
Both the lira and sterling were forced out of the ERM in September 1992 during a crisis which nearly led to its collapse.
The lira touched a two-year high on Thursday against the German mark at 989.20 and closed on Friday at 991.95.

France, which in the past has been sharply critical of the lira's depreciation and its competitive effects on French industry, praised Italy's efforts to reign in public spending, crucial to its hopes of joining monetary union in 1999.
ERM re-entry would be seen as a vote of confidence in Italy's ability to meet the preconditions of a common currency.

The EU's monetary committee, comprised of national treasury and central bank officials, meets on Tuesday for a regularly scheduled meeting. The agenda will focus on a budget stability pact among countries joining economic and monetary union (EMU).
There will also be a discussion on a new ERM, linking a single currency with those not qualifying for EMU in 1999.
While the lira may come up for discussion on Tuesday, officials say such deliberations normally take place over a special weekend meeting.
